issues.label: Jurisdiction and venue
issues.why: The court must confirm it has subject-matter jurisdiction and that venue was proper.

issues.label: Charging document sufficiency
issues.why: Each count must be properly alleged with all statutory elements and adequate notice.

issues.label: Double jeopardy protections
issues.why: Convictions and punishments cannot violate federal or state double-jeopardy rules.

issues.label: Merger: credit cards vs robbery
issues.why: The court must decide whether unlawful acquisition counts merge into aggravated robbery under Utah merger/double-punishment doctrine.

issues.label: Unit of prosecution: credit cards
issues.why: The court must determine whether each card supports a distinct count or whether acquisition in one episode is one offense.

issues.label: Unit of prosecution: sex acts
issues.why: The court must determine whether each distinct sexual act supports separate aggravated sexual assault counts.

issues.label: Aggravated sexual assault elements
issues.why: The court must ensure the evidence meets the elements for aggravated sexual assault (including the aggravator(s)).

issues.label: Aggravators: weapon/serious violence
issues.why: The court must confirm the aggravating factors (knife, strangulation, threats, injury) were proved as required.

issues.label: Aggravated assault elements
issues.why: The court must ensure the evidence supports aggravated assault separate from the sexual assaults.

issues.label: Aggravated assault as predicate act
issues.why: If assaultive conduct is used as an aggravator for sexual assault, the court must consider whether separate punishment is permissible.

issues.label: Aggravated robbery elements
issues.why: The court must confirm taking/attempted taking of car keys occurred by force or threat and meets aggravated robbery requirements.

issues.label: Robbery target: car keys
issues.why: The court must confirm the keys qualify as property and that the taking was sufficiently connected to force/threat.

issues.label: Credit-card acquisition elements
issues.why: The court must confirm each unlawful acquisition count meets statutory elements (obtain/possess/with required intent/means).

issues.label: Intent timing for theft offenses
issues.why: The court must determine when Connelley formed intent to steal keys/cards and whether it satisfies each offense.

issues.label: Consent as defense
issues.why: The court must address whether the sexual acts were nonconsensual beyond a reasonable doubt given conflicting testimony.

issues.label: Force/threat v consent analysis
issues.why: The court must assess whether strangulation/knife threats negate consent and establish compulsion elements.

issues.label: Credibility determinations limits
issues.why: At sentencing and on review, the court must ensure credibility assessments do not substitute for required legal findings at trial.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence (all counts)
issues.why: The court must ensure evidence was sufficient for each conviction under the governing standard.

issues.label: Inconsistent verdict concerns
issues.why: The court must consider whether any verdict inconsistency creates reversible legal error (typically it does not, but must be evaluated).

issues.label: Lesser-included offenses instructions
issues.why: The court must consider whether any lesser-included offense instructions were required or improperly omitted/given.

issues.label: Unanimity and jury instructions
issues.why: The court must ensure juror unanimity and instructions properly defined elements, consent, intent, and aggravators.

issues.label: Evidentiary admissibility issues
issues.why: The court must ensure any key evidence (victim statements, physical evidence, prior acts) was admitted/excluded under Utah rules.

issues.label: Confrontation/hearsay concerns
issues.why: Any testimonial hearsay admitted must satisfy confrontation requirements and evidentiary exceptions.

issues.label: Other-acts evidence (404(b))
issues.why: Any use of prior bad acts/criminal history at trial must satisfy permissible-purpose and balancing rules.

issues.label: Prosecutorial misconduct risk
issues.why: The court must consider whether argument about Connelley ‘victimizing people’ or similar themes was improper at trial (if raised).

issues.label: Ineffective assistance potential
issues.why: Counsel’s handling of merger, PSI inaccuracies, and sentencing objections may present Strickland issues.

issues.label: PSI accuracy obligations
issues.why: The court must address disputed PSI facts and comply with Utah requirements to resolve or disregard inaccuracies.

issues.label: Preservation of PSI objections
issues.why: The court must decide whether the defense adequately preserved PSI inaccuracy issues for appeal given counsel’s responses.

issues.label: Need for PSI findings on record
issues.why: If inaccuracies are alleged, the court must make findings or state it will not rely on disputed facts.

issues.label: Due process at sentencing
issues.why: Sentencing must not be based on materially false or unreliable information.

issues.label: Consideration of improper factors
issues.why: The court must ensure it did not punish Connelley for maintaining innocence or for protected speech, beyond permissible remorse considerations.

issues.label: Remorse/acceptance consideration limits
issues.why: The court may consider lack of remorse only within constitutional limits and not as a penalty for exercising trial rights.

issues.label: Victim impact evidence limits
issues.why: The court must ensure victim impact statements were considered appropriately and within statutory bounds.

issues.label: Sentencing range legality
issues.why: Each sentence must fall within the statutory minimum/maximum and correct degree/classification.

issues.label: Mandatory minimums applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether aggravated sexual assault required specific minimum terms and whether it applied them correctly.

issues.label: Consecutive sentencing authority
issues.why: The court must confirm statutory authority and standards for imposing consecutive sentences across counts and cases.

issues.label: Consecutive vs concurrent discretion
issues.why: The court must show it exercised discretion rather than applying a categorical policy for consecutive terms.

issues.label: Sentencing explanation adequacy
issues.why: The record must reflect consideration of required factors and a reasoned basis for consecutive maximum terms.

issues.label: Sentencing proportionality
issues.why: The court must ensure the overall sentence is not grossly disproportionate under constitutional standards.

issues.label: Public safety findings support
issues.why: Predictions of future dangerousness must be grounded in record evidence and permissible considerations.

issues.label: Consideration of age/mitigation
issues.why: The court must consider mitigation (age, circumstances) and ensure it was weighed, not ignored.

issues.label: Criminal history use at sentencing
issues.why: The court must ensure criminal history relied on is accurate and properly documented.

issues.label: Reliance on juvenile history
issues.why: If juvenile adjudications were considered, the court must ensure they were used permissibly and accurately.

issues.label: Multiple-victim consideration accuracy
issues.why: The court referenced ‘number of victims’; it must ensure this factor is factually correct and not overstated.

issues.label: Restitution considerations
issues.why: If restitution is at issue, the court must determine entitlement, amount, causation, and ability-to-pay procedures.

issues.label: Fees/fines/surcharges legality
issues.why: Any financial assessments must be authorized and imposed following required findings and procedures.

issues.label: Credit for time served
issues.why: The court must ensure correct jail/prison credit is awarded where required.

issues.label: Sex-offender collateral orders
issues.why: The court must ensure any required registration, testing, or treatment orders are imposed lawfully.

issues.label: Protective/no-contact orders
issues.why: Any protective order conditions must be authorized, properly entered, and not overbroad.

issues.label: Clerical accuracy of judgment
issues.why: The written judgment must match oral pronouncement, including concurrency, enhancements, and count designations.

issues.label: Sentencing across other cases
issues.why: Consecutive alignment to two other cases must be legally authorized and accurately reflected in all case judgments.

issues.label: Merger remedy selection
issues.why: If merger applies, the court must choose the correct remedy (vacatur of lesser counts/sentences) and adjust consecutive structure.

issues.label: Cumulative punishment analysis
issues.why: Even absent formal merger, the court must consider whether legislature authorized cumulative punishments for the charged combination.

issues.label: Standard of review and preservation
issues.why: On appeal, the court must determine applicable standards (plain error, harmless error, abuse of discretion) for each claim.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: If any error occurred (instructions, PSI, merger), the court must assess whether it was harmless beyond required standards.
